record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; source files and linked result documents were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports the outcome of a weight edit after quantization, bearing on whether an edit can remove refusals in a shipped model. It does not report a direct residual ablation reproduction.
record.gate_note: The README says Q4_K_M retained 55–98% of one edit's change on rude-llama and that refusals returned. The released-model table lists trials and links to result documents but gives no behavioral outcomes there. The described direction-extraction, search, and measurement procedures are not themselves reported outcomes.
record.test_reason: The README reports one result bearing on V2. On rude-llama, a weight edit quantized to Q4_K_M kept only 55–98% of its change, and refusals returned. The authors use this to argue that removal must be measured on the shipped quantized file, which qualifies V2. The repo is otherwise a tool, and its other outcomes sit in linked result files that were not provided.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue that an edit working on the 16-bit PyTorch model is not the shipped model, because quantization can round away part of a small edit. On rude-llama, Q4_K_M kept 55–98% of the change and refusals returned. Candor therefore scores and measures the exact quantized GGUF.
record.recipe_differences: A tool repo, not a stated replication. It describes difference-in-means directions, rank-1 LoRA edits, per-layer search, and measurement on exported quantized GGUFs rather than reporting the original direct ablation and addition procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Quantization is reported to affect edit retention and refusal behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Q4_K_M quantization retained 55–98% of one rank-1 edit's weight change on rude-llama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization can partially erase small refusal-removal weight edits.

record.problems: The README gives no refusal rate, uncertainty, or control for the quantization result, and the underlying linked result documents were not provided as text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcomes were left out. The released-model table gives model names and trial numbers but no measured behavioral values.

untested.parts: No reported ablation or addition result on refusal or on capabilities.
No refusal rates for the 16-bit edit, for other quantizations, or for the five released models in this text. Capability retention after the edit is not reported.
Thinking models (Qwen3.5-9B, K2-Horizon-7B, Qwen3.8-27B, Spark-X2.5-4B) are listed, but no outcomes appear in the README.

missing.what: Refusal rates and capability or maths measurements for the released exported GGUFs, compared with heretic. These bear on V2.
Results for direction removal in thinking models, and whether searching with thinking off is a valid proxy.
Effect of quantizing before versus after the edit on refusal.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tool repository with a README only; the source and result documents were not read. The single quantization result is anecdotal: no rate, no control, no uncertainty. The 'challenges' label proposed by the reader is too strong. The edit apparently worked before quantization, and its effect was only partly lost, so limits_scope fits. The tranche was changed from T2 to T5 because the result is an argument that V2 needs qualifying for quantized deployments.

versions.untested_parts: No reported direct ablation or addition result measuring refusal and other capabilities.
The README reports only a quantized edit on rude-llama, not refusal rates or results for the listed released models.
No reported result tests jailbreak suppression or robustness training.
No reported result compares a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No reported measurement separates harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No reported transfer result across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No reported comparison of how or when refusal training affects removability.
No reported result tests reasoning models against V1.
